newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH STATS OFFICIAL SAYS GDP FCAST TOO HIGH - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: CZECH STATS OFFICIAL SAYS GDP FCAST TOO HIGH - PAPER.

text.p: The Czech Statistical Bureau's (CSU) vice chairman Ivan Sujan said that the bureau's forecast of 1996 gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 4.8 percent might be too optimistic, a local daily reported on Tuesday
The daily Mlada Fronta Dnes quoted Sujan as saying a slowdown in growth was being caused by decreasing growth in of industrial production and lower export growth and investment.
"We have certain worries that the forecast (growth) indicator of GDP is a little bit too high," it quoted Sujan as saying.
The CSU originally forecast a 5.1 percent growth this year after 4.8 percent last year, but lowered the estimate to 4.8 percent in November.
"According to our so far unconfirmed thesis the pace of investment demand is also slowing down," Sujan added.

He said a slowdown in foreign capital inflow, lower profits of domestic companies and higher costs of credit following the central bank's tighter monetary policy earlier this year were to be blamed for the lower growth of investment demand.
Czech GDP grew 4.0 percent year-on-year in the second quarter of this year according to preliminary data, slowing from a 4.3 percent growth in the first quarter.
Industrial output rose 5.6 percent year-on-year in October, according to preliminary figures, after a 6.9 percent growth in September and a 19.5 percent growth in October 1995.
